# why's foxes

> A paperback copy of why's (poignant) Guide to Ruby travels to Ruby events as a guest book. People write on its pages. Pages with something for the whole community are scanned, optimized and posted on ruby.social as @whysfoxes, and this site collects those posts with transcripts, the people who wrote them and the replies.

- Each entry is one scanned page of the book, written on by one or more people. Page numbers are the printed page numbers of the paperback. Entries without a page number are mostly the title and front pages, and come first.
- Not every page is posted. Only pages that are at least partly meant for the whole community are. A thanks for a talk, or a plug for a library or a product, stays in the book.
- Every entry has a plain markdown version (the links below), with the community message, the post text, writers, chapter, event, notes and replies. The full transcript of the handwriting is only the alt text of the scan on the page.
- Writers are listed on every entry they wrote, with their profiles and their other entries. There are no separate pages for people.
- Everything is in one file at https://whysfoxes.github.io/whysfoxes_web/llms-full.txt if you would rather read it all at once.
- Illustrations from [why's (poignant) Guide to Ruby](https://poignant.guide/) by why the lucky stiff, [CC BY-SA 2.5](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/2.5/). Pages and scans from @whysfoxes@ruby.social. The handwriting belongs to the people who wrote it.

## Entries

### An untagged page by Yukihiro Matz Matsumoto, 2025-06-15

A page without a page number of why's (poignant) Guide to Ruby, the paperback guest book. Written by Yukihiro Matz Matsumoto. Scanned, optimized and posted on 2025-06-15.

#### Community message

> He started a movement.
> I miss you, why!
> まつもとゆきひろ
> matz

#### From the post on ruby.social

There, right at the front, just beneath the title and those gentle words that whisper who’s behind this masterpiece of a book (it’s why the lucky stiff, in case you’re still curious), you’ll find a little note from @matz addressed to  why:

It’s a note that feels like a secret handshake,
or a fox peeking out from behind a line of code.

> Happy (Rails) coding! Nice to see you at Ruby UnConf 2024!

#### From the post on ruby.social

Hey you!

Just flipped open the guestbook to the second page.
There, like a little post-it stuck to a monitor with a glob of code glue, @eileencodes left a note at @rubyunconf:

Now my book is smiling and my keyboard is jealous.
If you ever feel lonely, just remember:
Somewhere, a fox is coding,
a guestbook is winking,
and Eileen is cheering you on.

### Page 11 by Adam Wiggins, 2025-07-09

Page 11 of why's (poignant) Guide to Ruby, the paperback guest book. Written by Adam Wiggins. Scanned, optimized and posted on 2025-07-09.

#### Community message

> Keep up the Ruby-ing!

#### From the post on ruby.social

So @adamwiggins left a note in the 📔 book

Heroku and #Ruby go together like foxes and cleverness. Did you know #Heroku was born as a Ruby platform? In the early days, it was only for #Rubyists, #Rails and #gems, blocks & foxes, all running wild in the cloud.

So when Adam says “Keep up the Ruby-ing!” he’s really saying:
Let your gems sparkle, and remember that every Heroku #dyno is just a little fox,
waiting to carry your dreams into the cloud.

#### Image

![Scan of page 11](https://whysfoxes.github.io/whysfoxes_web/_astro/114823939372970525.3TPaeSb9_Z1RkSOb.jpeg)

#### Writers

- Adam Wiggins (@adamwiggins): [Mastodon](https://mas.to/@adamwiggins), [Bluesky](https://bsky.app/profile/adamwiggins.com), [RubyEvents](https://www.rubyevents.org/speakers/adam-wiggins).

### Page 68 by Sarah Mei, 2026-01-29

Page 68 of why's (poignant) Guide to Ruby, the paperback guest book. Written by Sarah Mei. It sits in [chapter 4](https://poignant.guide/book/chapter-4.html) of the book. Scanned, optimized and posted on 2026-01-29.

> Always be Ruby-friending!

#### From the post on ruby.social

On page 68 @sarahmei wrote a gentle reminder:

The foxes are nodding at each other,
swapping #gems like trading cards,
and every `def` feels like an invitation to 🍵 tea.

Ruby-friending isn't just about #code.
It's about the conversations in the hallway,
the debugging sessions that turn into laughter,
and the quiet moment when someone says "I get it now".

Every #Ruby #friend you make is another fox joining the den.

### Page 77 by Andy Croll, 2025-06-16

Page 77 of why's (poignant) Guide to Ruby, the paperback guest book. Written by Andy Croll. It sits in [chapter 5](https://poignant.guide/book/chapter-5.html) of the book. Written at Brighton Ruby. Scanned, optimized and posted on 2025-06-16.

#### Community message

> A: Go to Brighton Ruby. It’s really fun!
> B: I dunno, seems like we shouldn’t.

#### From the post on ruby.social

Found a chat between two foxes—just hanging out, like they own the place (and honestly, they do). Here’s what @andycroll, the wizard behind @brightonruby, scribbled:

They’ll probably say “no” at first, but that’s just fox logic.
Deep down, they’re already packing their bags,
sharpening their code,
and practising their best conference jokes.

#### From the post on ruby.social

On page 236, with a comic about adding a dividing slash to arrays, @eregon left a blessing with a little drawn gem:

The @truffleruby maintainer himself, wishing you the Truffle. The comic insists "RUBY doesn't come with this method! And skeletons don't come with beards. But wizards do!" A fox, neither skeleton nor wizard, accepts the truffle and moves on.
